:::: {.concept-card key="activation" tags="machine-learning"}
## activation

An intermediate value computed by a network for a particular input, as distinct from a learned parameter.
::::

:::: {.concept-card key="activation-function" tags="machine-learning"}
## activation function

A nonlinear function applied to a network's intermediate values, often elementwise.
It allows the network to represent nonlinear functions of its input.
::::

:::: {.concept-card key="autoregressive-generation" tags="machine-learning"}
## autoregressive generation

Generating an output sequence by repeatedly predicting the next element conditioned on earlier elements and any supplied context.
::::

:::: {.concept-card key="autoregressive-model" tags="machine-learning mathematics"}
## autoregressive model

A probability model that factorises a joint distribution into conditional distributions, each conditioned on earlier variables in a chosen order.
The variables may be discrete or continuous.
::::

:::: {.concept-card key="clipping" tags="machine-learning mathematics"}
## clipping

Replacing values outside a specified interval by its nearest endpoint.
Several distinct original values can then share the same result, so clipping generally cannot be inverted.
::::

:::: {.concept-card key="encoder" tags="machine-learning"}
## encoder

A function or model component that maps an input into a representation used by subsequent computation.
Its architecture and training objective determine what information the representation carries.
::::

:::: {.concept-card key="inference" tags="machine-learning"}
## inference

Using a trained model to compute predictions or generate outputs from supplied inputs.
Ordinary inference does not update the learned parameters.
::::

:::: {.concept-card key="learned-feature-vector" tags="machine-learning"}
## learned feature vector

A numerical description whose coordinates are produced or adjusted through learning for an objective.
The coordinates need not each correspond to a named human-interpretable property.
::::

:::: {.concept-card key="minibatch" tags="machine-learning"}
## minibatch

A group of training examples processed together to compute an update or shared batch statistics.
::::

:::: {.concept-card key="parameter" tags="machine-learning"}
## model parameter

A value that selects a model's behaviour, such as a learned weight or bias.
It is held fixed during an ordinary prediction, unlike the input.
::::

:::: {.concept-card key="parameterised-function" tags="machine-learning"}
## parameterised function

A family of functions indexed by parameters.
Fixing the parameters selects the function applied to an input.
::::

:::: {.concept-card key="probability-path" tags="machine-learning mathematics"}
## probability path

A family of probability distributions indexed by a time-like variable.
A generative flow chooses such a family to connect a simple starting distribution to a data distribution.
::::

:::: {.concept-card key="regularisation-penalty" tags="machine-learning mathematics"}
## regularisation penalty

An additional objective term that penalizes specified properties of parameters or predictions, expressing a preference beyond fitting the observed targets.
::::

:::: {.concept-card key="representation" tags="machine-learning"}
## representation

An encoding of information used by a model or computation.
Its form and usefulness depend on what later operations need to do with it.
::::

:::: {.concept-card key="sampler" tags="machine-learning mathematics"}
## sampler

A procedure for producing draws from, or approximating draws from, a specified distribution.
It includes the random inputs and numerical update rules, not only the trained network.
::::

:::: {.concept-card key="score" tags="machine-learning mathematics"}
## score of a density

The gradient of log density with respect to the sample coordinates.
It indicates the local direction and rate of increase of log density, and differs from a gradient with respect to model parameters.
::::

:::: {.concept-card key="softmax" tags="machine-learning"}
## softmax

A function that exponentiates scores and divides each exponential by their sum, producing positive values that sum to one for finite scores.
::::

:::: {.concept-card key="teacher-forcing" tags="machine-learning"}
## teacher forcing

Training a sequence predictor using the observed earlier outputs as context for later predictions.
Generation usually supplies the model’s own earlier outputs instead.
::::

:::: {.concept-card key="token" tags="machine-learning"}
## token

A sequence element processed by a model.
Depending on the input path, it may originate from a discrete vocabulary item or a continuous feature vector.
::::

:::: {.concept-card key="training-objective" tags="machine-learning mathematics"}
## training objective

A scalar-valued function of model parameters that the training procedure seeks to optimize, often combining data loss and additional penalties.
::::

:::: {.concept-card key="transformer" tags="machine-learning"}
## transformer

A neural-network architecture built from blocks that combine attention with positionwise transformations, typically using residual connections and normalization.
::::

:::: {.concept-card key="velocity-field" tags="machine-learning mathematics"}
## velocity field

A function assigning a local direction and rate of change to each position and time.
In flow generation, it changes a sample with respect to internal generative time.
::::
